limits: A valid receipt says each party’s key signed its own part and the parts chain. It does not say any party told the truth.

The carried keys are the parties’ only if the verifier already holds those key_ids from somewhere else. A receipt cannot vouch for its own keys. When two roles are signed by one key, one holder signed both.
The acceptance names who accepted. The signature proves the acceptor’s key signed the receipt, not that the person named did.
money none means no money is held or paid by this receipt.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a receipt that still verifies.
The checks prove only what they test. A passed record says the pinned commands exited 0 on that tree, not that the work is good.
A test that cannot fail is not detected by this record.

The checker ran them as recorded only as far as the verifier trusts the checker’s key. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued the record, and content_hash that it was not edited since; the carried key is the checker’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a record that still verifies.
A delivery says what the doer’s Tick recorded handing in, not that the work is right. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued it, and content_hash that it was not edited since.
cents marked reported came from the agent’s platform and were not measured.
It does not prove the order exists or that this delivery answers it; that is checked where a receipt binds the two.
The carried key is the doer’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else. A delivery cannot vouch for its own key.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a delivery that still verifies.
A work order says what was asked, not that anything was done. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued it, and content_hash that it was not edited since.
The carried key is the buyer’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else. A work order cannot vouch for its own key.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a work order that still verifies.
payment none means no money is held for this order.

Finding F5 of NOTE-mvro4w8x (decisions GD-82, GD-83). The land gate (packages/runner/src/ticked-gate.ts) asks the coordinator for a task's signed receipt of version two before the land step runs, and that receipt needs the landing the land step itself records afterwards, so it refused every landing of work created after the ticked line (seen on 2026-10-28; PARSA took ticked-line.json off main by hand to get out). Its module comment says the coordinator "signs and records it when first asked": that holds for the work order, not for this receipt. The coordinator's half has landed with the task this one depends on: `GET /v1/runs/:id/tasks/:taskId/receipt-v2/ready` answers 200 `{ ready: true, run_id, task_id }` or the receipt route's own refusals, signing and recording nothing. Read packages/api/src/task-receipt-v2-route.ts as it stands on main to see it. This task is the runner's half.

THE CHANGE.
1. packages/runner/src/project-calls.ts: `receiptReadyWith(send, refusal, runId, taskId)` like `receiptV2With`, for `/v1/runs/${runId}/tasks/${taskId}/receipt-v2/ready`, typed `unknown`.
2. packages/runner/src/http-coordinator-client.ts: a method `getTaskReceiptReady(runId, taskId)` beside `getTaskReceiptV2`. This file is AT its ratchet baseline (file-size-baseline.json, 3176 lines) and may not grow (`node scripts/file-size-ratchet.mjs` holds it): make the room inside this file, for example by removing comments that restate a signature (CLAUDE.md, "Doc-comment scope"), and say in your report what you shortened. If it cannot be done without growing the file, stop and report that, do not raise the baseline.
3. packages/runner/src/ticked-gate.ts: `ReceiptReader` gets an optional `getTaskReceiptReady`, and `tickedFor` asks that instead of `getTaskReceiptV2`. The module comment and the names say what is true: the gate asks whether the work is ready for a receipt (everything the receipt holds but the landing), not for the receipt; `tick landings` stays the proof afterwards. The refusal still carries LAND_UNTICKED and names each task with the coordinator's words as now; a client that cannot ask refuses every task, as now. The module comment may not grow.
4. Tests. Update packages/runner/src/ticked-gate.test.ts and packages/runner/src/landing-provider-ticked.test.ts. Their stand-in coordinator must behave like the real one, which the first tests did not: its `getTaskReceiptV2` REJECTS (409, fact "landing") until the land step has landed, while `getTaskReceiptReady` answers. Prove with it that a landing carrying a task created after the line goes through, and that one whose task the stand-in says is not ready (for example, no work order) is refused with LAND_UNTICKED, and that a task created before the line is still not asked. Add a NEW file packages/runner/src/http-coordinator-client-ready.test.ts (http-coordinator-client.test.ts is 3045 lines and cannot grow) that proves the request goes to `/receipt-v2/ready` with the signed GET and that a refusal is mapped as the receipt route's is. Each assertion must be able to fail: change the code to check.

CONSTRAINTS. packages/runner/src/coordinator-dispatch.ts is 497 lines and must not grow; it should need no change, because it hands the gate the same client. Existing tests are edited only where this change breaks them, and the report lists them. A source file stays under 500 lines. Touch no other file.
